extra_vocab.zh: 承認；確認收到；表示感謝
extra_vocab.en: to accept or say that something is true, or to say you have received it
extra_vocab.note: 在商務情境裡語氣中性又正式：可以是承認問題或錯誤，也可以是「確認收到」某封信或訂單。讀到 acknowledge 時，先看後面接的是事實、錯誤，還是 receipt。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: acknowledge 後面可接名詞、that 子句或 V-ing（如 acknowledge receiving），不接 to V。

example.en: The system acknowledges every order as soon as it arrives.
example.zh: 系統一收到訂單就會確認每一筆。

example.en: The manager acknowledged the delay and apologized to the client.
example.zh: 經理承認有延誤，並向客戶道歉。

example.en: Thank you for acknowledging our request so quickly.
example.zh: 謝謝你這麼快就回覆確認我們的要求。

example.en: Please acknowledge receipt of this email by replying today.
example.zh: 請於今天回信，確認收到這封郵件。

example.en: It is important to acknowledge a mistake and fix it quickly.
example.zh: 承認錯誤並盡快改正很重要。

example.en: The team acknowledged the importance of clear communication with clients.
example.zh: 團隊肯定與客戶清楚溝通的重要性。

example.en: We acknowledge that the delivery was late this month.
example.zh: 我們承認本月的出貨延遲了。

examples.en: We acknowledge your order and will ship it on Monday.
examples.zh: 我們已確認收到您的訂單，會在星期一出貨。

examples.en: The director acknowledged that the project needed more time.
examples.zh: 主管承認這個專案需要更多時間。

examples.en: The company acknowledged the problem and offered a full refund.
examples.zh: 公司承認有問題，並提供全額退款。

examples.en: I would like to acknowledge everyone who helped on this project.
examples.zh: 我想感謝所有協助這個專案的人。

confusable.diff: knowledge 是名詞「知識」；acknowledge 是動詞「承認、確認」，字裡包含 knowledge，容易拼錯。
confusable.usage: knowledge 是不可數名詞，不加 s；acknowledge 是動詞，前面多了 ac-。

example.en: Her knowledge of the market helped us win the contract.
example.zh: 她對市場的了解幫助我們贏得合約。

similar.diff: admit 多半指承認不好的事（錯誤、失敗）；acknowledge 較中性、較正式，也能表示確認收到。

example.en: He admitted that the report had several serious errors.
example.zh: 他承認這份報告有幾個嚴重的錯誤。

similar.diff: recognize 常指認出某人或肯定某人的價值；acknowledge 重點在公開承認或表示收到。

example.en: The company recognized her work with a special award.
example.zh: 公司以特別獎肯定她的工作表現。

example.en: Please confirm the meeting time by tomorrow morning.
example.zh: 請在明天早上前確認會議時間。

example.en: The client accepted our offer after a short discussion.
example.zh: 客戶在簡短討論後接受了我們的報價。

example.en: Please respond to this email as soon as you can.
example.zh: 請盡快回覆這封電子郵件。

example.en: We appreciate your patience while we fix the problem.
example.zh: 感謝您在我們處理問題期間的耐心。

derived.link: acknowledge + -ment，把動作變成名詞，像 payment、agreement。也可拼成 acknowledgement。

senses.en: to say that something is true, especially something bad

example.en: The CEO acknowledged that sales had dropped last quarter.
example.zh: 執行長承認上一季的銷售下滑了。

senses.en: to tell someone you have received their message or package
senses.distinguish: 後面通常接 receipt of 或信件、訂單等名詞。

example.en: Please acknowledge the package as soon as it arrives.
example.zh: 包裹一到，請立刻確認收到。

senses.en: to thank someone or show that you value their work
senses.distinguish: 後面接人或貢獻，情境多為致謝或表揚。

example.en: The report acknowledges the help of the finance team.
example.zh: 這份報告對財務團隊的協助表示感謝。

extra_vocab.zh: 出現、發生（問題）；被提起；即將到來
extra_vocab.en: to happen or appear, often without a plan
extra_vocab.note: 文章裡 when something comes up 指工作中「臨時冒出來」的問題，這時需要 critical thinking 來處理。口語也常用 something came up 表示「臨時有事」。
extra_vocab.pattern: N + come(s) up / if something comes up
extra_vocab.grammar_note: if 或 when 子句裡用現在式代替未來式，如 If something comes up, call me（不說 will come up）。

examples.en: A new problem came up during the meeting this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上開會時出現了一個新問題。

examples.en: Sorry, something came up, so I need to move our call.
examples.zh: 抱歉，臨時有事，我需要改一下通話時間。

examples.en: The budget question came up again in today's discussion.
examples.zh: 預算的問題在今天的討論中又被提起了。

examples.en: Our busiest season is coming up in the next two weeks.
examples.zh: 我們最忙的季節在接下來兩週就要到了。

examples.en: If any questions come up, please contact me directly.
examples.zh: 如果有任何問題，請直接與我聯絡。

similar.diff: arise 較正式，常用在書面；come up 比較口語自然。

example.en: Problems may arise if we change the schedule again.
example.zh: 如果我們再改一次時程，可能會出現問題。

similar.diff: happen 單純指事情發生；come up 常指臨時冒出、需要處理的事。

example.en: Something happened at the factory, so we closed early.
example.zh: 工廠發生了一些事，所以我們提早關門。

confusable.diff: come up with 是「想出（點子、方案）」；come up 單獨用是「出現、發生」。
confusable.usage: come up with 後面一定要接受詞（想出的東西）；come up 是不及物，後面不接受詞。

example.en: She came up with a clever plan to cut shipping costs.
example.zh: 她想出了一個降低運費的聰明辦法。

confusable.diff: come across 是偶然遇見或發現；come up 是事情出現或被提起。

example.en: I came across an old file while cleaning my desk.
example.zh: 我在整理桌面時偶然發現一個舊檔案。

extra_vocab.en: useful and sensible in real situations
extra_vocab.note: 文章裡提到 strategic thinking 需要多練習（practice）。practical 和 practice 同字族，意思是「在實際情況中有用、可行」，常拿來和 theory（理論）對比。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: practical 是形容詞，修飾名詞；名詞或動詞「練習」是 practice，不要寫成 practical。

example.en: The job requires two years of practical experience in sales.
example.zh: 這份工作需要兩年的銷售實務經驗。

example.en: We found a practical solution to the delivery problem.
example.zh: 我們找到了解決出貨問題的可行辦法。

example.en: The workshop gave us practical advice on time management.
example.zh: 這場工作坊給了我們時間管理的實用建議。

example.en: Training should build practical skills, not just theory.
example.zh: 訓練應該培養實作技能，而不只是理論。

examples.en: Let's choose the most practical way to reduce our costs.
examples.zh: 我們來選一個最可行的方法降低成本。

examples.en: This tool is small, light, and very practical for travel.
examples.zh: 這個工具又小又輕，出差帶著非常實用。

examples.en: Thank you for your practical suggestions on the new schedule.
examples.zh: 謝謝你對新時程提出實用的建議。

confusable.diff: practice 是名詞或動詞「練習、實務」；practical 是形容詞「實用的」。
confusable.usage: practice 當動詞時，英式拼成 practise；practical 只能當形容詞，後面接名詞。

example.en: Regular practice helps new staff learn the system faster.
example.zh: 規律的練習能幫助新員工更快學會系統。

similar.diff: realistic 強調符合現實、不誇張；practical 強調好用、做得到。

example.en: We set a realistic goal for next quarter's sales.
example.zh: 我們為下一季的銷售設定了切合實際的目標。

similar.diff: useful 是一般的「有用」；practical 更強調實際可行、好操作。

example.en: This report is useful for planning next year's budget.
example.zh: 這份報告對規劃明年預算很有用。

example.en: The new office is convenient for staff who take the train.
example.zh: 新辦公室對搭火車的員工很方便。

example.en: Your comments on the draft were very helpful.
example.zh: 你對草稿的意見很有幫助。

example.en: Cutting waste is a sensible way to save money.
example.zh: 減少浪費是省錢的明智方法。

example.en: An efficient process saves time for the whole team.
example.zh: 有效率的流程能替整個團隊省時間。

derived.link: 這是詞幹。practice + -al，變成「和實務有關的」，也就是 practical。
im- 表示「不」，像 impossible，加在 practical 前面變相反。

senses.en: useful and easy to use in daily life

example.en: A small desk lamp is practical for working late.
example.zh: 小型桌燈很適合晚上加班時使用。

senses.en: about real actions, not only ideas

example.en: The course offers practical training instead of only theory.
example.zh: 這門課提供實作訓練，而不只是理論。

senses.en: good at dealing with real problems in a sensible way
senses.distinguish: 修飾的是人，如 a practical person。

example.en: Our manager is practical and always asks about the budget.
example.zh: 我們經理很務實，總是會問預算。

extra_vocab.zh: 完全地、絕對地；當然（回答用）
extra_vocab.note: 文章裡 you absolutely need that as a skill 用 absolutely 加強語氣，表示「絕對需要」。它放在動詞 need 前面，讓這句話更強烈。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: absolutely 常搭配 essential、necessary、certain 這類本身已很強的字；不和 very 連用，也不說 absolutely small 這種分級形容詞。

example.en: It is absolutely necessary to back up the data every day.
example.zh: 每天備份資料是絕對必要的。

example.en: Clear communication is absolutely essential for a remote team.
example.zh: 對遠端團隊來說，清楚的溝通絕對不可或缺。

example.en: I am absolutely certain that the payment was sent.
example.zh: 我完全確定款項已經寄出了。

example.en: Can we skip the safety check? Absolutely not.
example.zh: 我們可以跳過安全檢查嗎？絕對不行。

examples.en: We absolutely must finish the plan before the end of the month.
examples.zh: 我們絕對必須在月底前完成計畫。

examples.en: Absolutely! I can send you the report this afternoon.
examples.zh: 沒問題！我今天下午就可以把報告寄給你。

examples.en: You are absolutely right, and we are sorry for the mistake.
examples.zh: 您說得完全正確，對於這個錯誤我們深感抱歉。

confusable.diff: absolute 是形容詞「絕對的、完全的」；absolutely 是副詞，修飾動詞或形容詞。
confusable.usage: absolute 放在名詞前（absolute trust）；absolutely 放在動詞前或形容詞前。

example.en: We have absolute trust in our new supplier.
example.zh: 我們對新供應商有絕對的信任。

similar.diff: definitely 表示「肯定地、一定」，用來確認或保證；absolutely 的語氣更強，表示完全。

example.en: I will definitely call you after the client meeting.
example.zh: 客戶會議結束後，我一定會打電話給你。

similar.diff: totally 較口語；absolutely 在書面和口語都能用，語氣較正式。

example.en: I totally agree with your plan for the launch.
example.zh: 我完全同意你對產品上市的規劃。

example.en: The old system was completely replaced last week.
example.zh: 舊系統上週已被完全換掉。

example.en: The delay was entirely caused by bad weather.
example.zh: 這次延誤完全是壞天氣造成的。

example.en: The deadline is extremely tight for the whole team.
example.zh: 這個期限對整個團隊來說極度緊迫。

example.en: The room is fully booked for the training session.
example.zh: 這間會議室已被培訓課程完全訂滿。

derived.link: 這是詞幹。absolute + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 quick → quickly。

example.en: We absolutely need your approval before we start the work.
example.zh: 開工前我們絕對需要您的核准。

example.en: Can you join the call? Absolutely, I will be there.
example.zh: 你能加入通話嗎？當然，我會到。
